en.title: Maximum Types Kept After Clearing R Consecutive Shelves
en.description:
Clear exactly R consecutive shelves without changing the order of the other shelves, and find the maximum number of distinct types among the remaining shelves. The original site's answer of 2 for the first example is incorrect; this site corrected it to 3 according to the definition.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.input: The first line contains N R (1≤N≤100000, 1≤R≤N), and the second line contains N types (1..100000).
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: after deleting 0-based indices 2, 3, 4, the remaining 2, 1, 3, 2 keep three types, which is all three types of the original array; the original site's answer of 2 missed this option.

Example 2: deleting the last 2 cells leaves 2, 3, 1, keeping 3 types.

Example 3: all shelves are deleted and no type remains, so the answer is 0.
hints: First subtract the first deletion window from the global frequencies, then slide the window: restore the old left end, delete the new right end, and maintain the number of types whose remaining frequency is positive.
